title: JSON-driven tool parameter coercion, diagnostic hints, and graceful compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: runtime tool/function calls rely on JSON schemas to validate params. Current validation modes are brittle: either reject too aggressively (breaking older clients) or accept everything (leading to silent mis-invocations and hard-to-debug errors). We need a single, opt-in schema format and runtime behavior that enables: 1) deterministic coercion rules for common mismatches (number-as-string, optional single-item arrays), 2) a compact, human-friendly error taxonomy with actionable hints, and 3) a compatibility shim to let older SDKs continue working while encouraging authors to adopt stricter contracts.
technical_notes:
Design principles: prefer predictable, auditable coercions over magic; always preserve original input in diagnostic payloads; surface a single canonical error code per failing param and a short "suggested fix" string. Modes: 
- permissive (default for hosted API v1): apply conservative coercions, emit warnings (validation_warning telemetry), return structured diagnostic with code:warning instead of 4xx where possible.
- strict (opt-in via route or model config): reject on first schema violation and return structured error code with path.
Coercion rules (proposed):
- number/string: trim and parse numeric strings when schema expects number; fail if NaN.
- boolean: accept true/false, "true"/"false", 1/0 only when coercion enabled.
- single-item arrays: if schema expects array and input is scalar, coerce to [value] if element type matches after coercion.
- enums: case-insensitive match when schema flag case_insensitive_enum=true.
Diagnostic hints: each error object should include: code (short token), path (dotpath), original_value (stringified), suggested_fix (short text), docs_link (short URL).
Compatibility shim: when request includes header X-RW-Compat:legacy allow older parameter names mapped via a simple alias list delivered in model/tool manifest. Runtime should log alias usage and emit warning metrics.
Telemetry: capture validation_result: {ok|warn|fail}, coercions_applied:int, errors:[codes], alias_hits:int. Ensure PII is not captured in logs; only stringified hashes allowed for big payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Define a JSON schema extension (spec fragment) that adds: coercion_profile:string, case_insensitive_enum:boolean, aliases:list of {from,to}.
2) Implement permissive and strict runtime paths in the serving runtime and JS/Go SDKs.
3) Validation outputs include the diagnostic hint fields and stable error codes documented in the public API reference.
4) Add telemetry counters and a Grafana dashboard (validation rate, coercion rate, alias hits, error distribution).
5) Rollout: feature flag guarded, canary enabled for 10% of hosted API traffic and Dedicated customers with opt-in.
6) Backward-compat: older SDKs using alias headers continue to succeed in permissive mode; strict mode must return 4xx with error code VALIDATION_STRICT_FAILURE.
7) Add 40 unit tests and 6 integration tests covering coercions and alias resolution.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): spec + SDK prototype + unit tests behind feature flag (2 weeks). Phase 2 (canary): enable permissive mode for 10% hosted + 2 Dedicated customers, collect telemetry and error samples (2 weeks). Phase 3 (opt-in strict): allow projects to flip strict=true per-route; collect regression metrics and add migration guide (3 weeks). Phase 4 (default switch): evaluate after 8 weeks of canary; if key metrics stable, consider promoting stricter linting in authoring tools. Each phase must include a rollback tag and runbook.
testing_notes: Unit tests: validate coercion matrix (number/string/boolean/array/enum). Integration: send mixed-version client requests with aliases header and verify success in permissive mode and failure in strict. Load test: ensure validation path adds <2% CPU overhead at p95 for average payload sizes. Security: schema handling must avoid entity expansion and limit recursion depth in schema resolution. Add fuzzing harness for malformed JSON and very large arrays.
